cards.front: At 19 weeks, monochorionic diamniotic twins have fluid pockets of 9 cm and 1 cm. The donor bladder remains unseen throughout the scan; Dopplers are normal, and neither twin has hydrops. The Quintero classification is [___].
cards.context:
Fluid discordance establishes the syndrome; loss of the donor bladder moves it beyond stage I.

Normal Dopplers and no hydrops exclude stages III and IV. Staging describes findings, not an inevitable stepwise sequence.

cards.front: Anticoagulant of choice throughout pregnancy is [___]; warfarin is teratogenic at 6-12 weeks; DOACs are contraindicated.
cards.context:
LMWH does not cross the placenta, so it is the anticoagulant of choice in pregnancy. After birth, LMWH or warfarin is compatible with breastfeeding.

Warfarin crosses the placenta and is most teratogenic at 6-12 weeks; later exposure risks fetal intracranial bleeding.

Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) lack pregnancy safety data and are contraindicated. Use indication- and weight-appropriate LMWH dosing under the relevant protocol.

cards.front: At 28 weeks, a woman undergoes a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test: fasting glucose is 5.3 mmol/L, while both post-load results are below diagnostic thresholds. Under ADIPS 2025, the diagnosis is [___].
cards.context: One qualifying result establishes GDM; normal post-load results do not cancel a fasting value at the threshold. Calling the test normal is the trap.

cards.front: A fetus on a CTG has reassuring variability of about [___] bpm, showing an intact autonomic system.
cards.context: Reassuring variability is about 6 to 25 beats per minute. It shows the fetal autonomic system is intact.

cards.front: A pregnant woman with asymptomatic vasa praevia attends specialist antenatal care and has no risk factors for preterm birth. Planned caesarean birth can be considered from [___] of gestation.
cards.context:
In asymptomatic vasa praevia with no risk factors for preterm birth, consider caesarean birth from 36+0 weeks.

If preterm-birth risk factors are present, consider it from 34+0 weeks instead.

cards.front: Restitution realigns the delivered head with the [___].
cards.context: The head turns after emergence to align with the shoulders, which are still within the birth canal. This is part of the normal sequence of vaginal birth.

cards.front: Because mesh exposure offsets its benefit, a first anterior prolapse repair uses [___].
cards.context:
Fewer returning bulges are not a free win. The same mesh that holds the anterior wall can come through the vagina, and the combined return-to-theatre rate is higher.

That trade-off is why a first repair stays with native tissue. Mesh is not forbidden forever, but it is not the opening operation.

cards.front: Haemoglobin concentration falls in normal pregnancy even though red-cell mass rises, because [___] expands proportionally more.
cards.context:
Plasma volume rises by about 40-50%, red-cell mass by only about 20-30%. Haemoglobin concentration therefore falls even though total red-cell mass has increased.

The extra volume protects against blood loss at birth. Iron deficiency is still common and needs checking.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation adrenaline (HR persistently <[___] despite PPV + compressions): 0.1-0.3 mL/kg of 1:10,000 IV via umbilical venous catheter (UVC).
cards.context:
Adrenaline in neonatal resus is reserved for persistent HR <60 despite effective PPV + chest compressions for ≥30 sec.

Ventilation remains the priority — adrenaline without effective ventilation is futile in respiratory-arrest physiology.

Volume expansion (10 mL/kg saline) for hypovolaemia; glucose only if confirmed hypoglycaemia.

cards.front: At 32 weeks, a previously normotensive woman has confirmed hypertension and newly diagnosed placental insufficiency with fetal growth restriction. Proteinuria is absent; the maternal diagnosis is [___].
cards.context: New organ involvement can establish pre-eclampsia without proteinuria. Gestational hypertension is the trap when placental dysfunction is overlooked.

cards.front: With a normal hip examination but DDH risk factors, screening hip ultrasound is commonly arranged at about [___]; confirmed DDH may be treated with a specialist-directed Pavlik harness.
cards.context:
With normal examination but breech presentation or first-degree family history, use the local screening pathway. An unstable newborn hip needs prompt senior/orthopaedic assessment, not delayed screening.

Treatment depends on confirmed findings and age. A Pavlik harness is one specialist-directed option in young infants. [RCH DDH](https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedFiles/Main/Content/ortho/factsheets/DDH.pdf).

cards.front: EPDS interpretation thresholds: a total score of [___] is the cut-off for probable depression (full psychiatric assessment); scores of 10-12 are possible cases (repeat in 2-4 weeks); a positive response on the dedicated self-harm item triggers immediate safety assessment regardless of total score.
cards.context:
EPDS is a 10-item self-report questionnaire (scored 0-30) validated for antenatal + postnatal screening.

Interpretation: <10 = low risk, routine follow-up; 10-12 = possible, repeat in 2-4 weeks; ≥13 = probable, full psychiatric assessment.

cards.front: PPROM (preterm prelabour rupture of membranes) diagnosis: history of fluid gush + [___] examination showing pooling of amniotic fluid; avoid digital vaginal exam (raises infection risk, shortens latency).
cards.context:
The 'no digital VE in PPROM' rule is a key safety rule: each digital exam introduces vaginal flora into the cervix and through ruptured membranes, raising chorioamnionitis risk + shortening latency by hours.

Use sterile speculum instead — visualises cervix + pooling without entering the os. If labour established and you need dilatation, a single careful digital exam may be unavoidable — document the indication.

'Gush' history is sensitive but not specific (urinary incontinence, discharge, amniocentesis leak can mimic) — confirm with speculum + IGFBP-1/PAMG-1 if uncertain.

cards.front: The PITCHES trial (2019) showed ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) does not reduce adverse perinatal outcomes in intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP); the most important intervention is [___] timing based on bile acid level.
cards.context:
UDCA was the standard ICP treatment for decades on observational evidence.

UDCA remains widely used for symptomatic relief but focus shifted to delivery timing as the single most outcome-influencing intervention.

Weekly bile acid monitoring catches escalating disease.

cards.front: A diastolic pressure of 110 mmHg or more in pregnancy is [___].
cards.context:
NSW ACI 2026: systolic 160 mmHg or more, or diastolic 110 mmHg or more, is severe hypertension. Do not wait for both numbers to cross the threshold.

Confirmation uses three consecutive measurements at least two minutes apart. Severe hypertension requires immediate escalation and treatment.

cards.front: A woman has repeated BP readings above 160/110 mmHg. She feels well; blood results are pending. Request urgent [___] treatment with maternal monitoring.
cards.context: NSW ACI 2026: the supplied severe BP is sufficient to require urgent assessment and treatment. Do not infer reassuring laboratory findings from their absence.

cards.front: At 27 weeks, a 75 g OGTT gives fasting 5.2, 1-hour 9.8 and 2-hour 8.1 mmol/L. Under ADIPS 2025, gestational diabetes is [___].
cards.context:
The 2014 fasting threshold was 5.1 mmol/L; ADIPS 2025 raised it to 5.3. Post-load thresholds are now 10.6 at 1 hour and 9.0 at 2 hours.

A fasting 5.2 with normal post-load values was diabetes under the old criteria but is not under the new ones.

cards.front: Among the 4 Ts of postpartum haemorrhage, the commonest cause, at about 70% of cases, is uterine atony, and a retained placenta falls under [___].
cards.context:
Tone (uterine atony) causes about 70% of PPH, Trauma (genital-tract lacerations) about 20%, Tissue (retained placenta or products) about 10%, and Thrombin (coagulopathy) about 1%.

NSW defines PPH as blood loss of at least 500 mL whatever the mode of birth. Uterotonics and uterine massage treat atony first.

cards.front: In pre-eclampsia, significant proteinuria on a 24-hour urine collection is at least [___].
cards.context:
A spot urine protein:creatinine ratio of 30 mg/mmol or more is the quicker equivalent.

Proteinuria is not required for the diagnosis: new hypertension with maternal end-organ or fetal involvement also counts.

cards.front: A baby lying bottom-first or feet-first, rather than head-first, is in a [___] presentation.
cards.context:
This is the presentation in which the buttocks or the feet lead, instead of the head.

Labour and birth then carry more risk of harm from trauma or lack of oxygen than a head-first labour.

That difference is why the type of breech and the baby's size change whether a vaginal birth can be planned.

cards.front: Among the 4 Ts of postpartum haemorrhage, the commonest cause, at about 70% of cases, is [___], and a retained placenta falls under Tissue.
cards.context:
Tone (uterine atony) causes about 70% of PPH, Trauma (genital-tract lacerations) about 20%, Tissue (retained placenta or products) about 10%, and Thrombin (coagulopathy) about 1%.

NSW defines PPH as blood loss of at least 500 mL whatever the mode of birth. Uterotonics and uterine massage treat atony first.

cards.front: Non-severe hypertension in pregnancy is SBP ≥[___] and/or DBP ≥90 mmHg, confirmed with repeat measurements on 2 occasions at least four hours apart.
cards.context:
Use correct technique and repeated readings. SOMANZ advises three readings about two minutes apart, with reassessment at least four hours later for non-severe hypertension.

SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110 mmHg needs prompt repeat assessment and urgent obstetric escalation; do not wait four hours. Assess symptoms and organ involvement as well as BP.

Hypertension before 20 weeks suggests chronic hypertension. After 20 weeks, distinguish gestational hypertension from pre-eclampsia using maternal and fetal assessment.

cards.front: A T-piece device needs working [___], so a self-inflating bag is kept beside it if that delivery fails.
cards.context:
The T-piece is suggested because pressure and oxygen can be set and watched. Those breaths stop if the wall gas or the hose fails.

A flow-inflating bag has the same weakness. The self-inflating bag still refills from the room, which is why it stays on the cot.

cards.front: After an abnormal auscultation, a cardiotocograph is normal, with no maternal or fetal risk factors and a reassuring clinical assessment. Consider returning to [___].
cards.context:
If cardiotocography is normal after an abnormal auscultation finding and no maternal or fetal risk factors remain, intermittent auscultation may be resumed.

The woman's overall risk and the reason for the original concern still guide the decision.

cards.front: Empirical antibiotics for early-onset neonatal sepsis: [___] (covers GBS) + gentamicin (covers Gram-negatives like E. coli); stop at 36-48 hours if cultures negative + well.
cards.context:
EONS (<72 h) is dominated by vertically transmitted maternal flora — GBS and E. coli account for ~70%.

Empirical antibiotics target both: benzylpenicillin (GBS, Listeria, syphilis) + gentamicin (E. coli and other Gram-negatives, synergistic with penicillin against GBS); doses benzylpen 60 mg/kg IV 12-hourly.

LONS (>72 h) more often nosocomial — flucloxacillin (Staph) + gent. Add aciclovir 20 mg/kg IV 8-hourly if HSV suspected (vesicles, focal neurology, maternal active genital herpes).

cards.front: Preconception [___] supplementation reduces the risk of fetal neural tube defects.
cards.context:
The classic preconception intervention: start BEFORE conception and continue through the first trimester, when the neural tube closes.

High-dose is used for higher-risk women (previous NTD, diabetes, certain medications).

cards.front: The first manoeuvre for shoulder dystocia is the [___] manoeuvre (hyperflexing the maternal hips).
cards.context:
Shoulder dystocia is a 'no traction' emergency.

The first and often sufficient manoeuvre is McRoberts (hyperflex maternal hips onto the abdomen) plus suprapubic pressure — it rotates the pelvis to free the anterior shoulder.

cards.front: In suspected ovarian torsion, normal colour Doppler flow does not exclude the diagnosis because torsion can be intermittent; proceed to [___] if clinical suspicion is high.
cards.context:
The Doppler trap in ovarian torsion is intermittent flow.

Time to detorsion matters, but a dark, congested ovary often recovers. Detorse and conserve the ovary even after delayed presentation; oophorectomy is rarely needed.

So when the clinical picture is right (sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain, peritonism, vomiting, adnexal mass on imaging) — go straight to laparoscopy.

cards.front: Initial intrauterine resuscitation for prolonged fetal bradycardia: maternal repositioning and stop uterotonics; if persistent, proceed to category 1 [___].
cards.context:
Prolonged fetal bradycardia (FHR <110 for >3 min) is a peripartum emergency. If unresolved by 9 min or with an abnormal CTG, proceed to category 1 caesarean.

Caesarean urgency (RANZCOG): Cat 1 = immediate threat to mother/fetus, deliver ≤30 min; Cat 2 = compromise without immediate threat, ≤75 min; Cat 3 = early delivery, no compromise; Cat 4 = elective.

cards.front: Ongoing postpartum blood loss of at least 1500 mL is an indication to activate the local [___] protocol.
cards.context:
NSW GL2025_013: ongoing bleeding with loss ≥1500 mL triggers the massive haemorrhage protocol. Clinical deterioration warrants urgent help regardless of whether a volume threshold has been reached.

Blood tests do not replace clinical assessment.
